newsitem.title: FRANCE: Usinor-Sacilor sees lower prices in H1 97.
newsitem.headline: Usinor-Sacilor sees lower prices in H1 97.

text.p: French steelmaker Usinor Sacilor said on Tuesday that while volumes were up significantly, average prices "at least for the first half of the year should be lower than they were in 1996".

The company which reported that 1996 profits slid to 1.49 billion francs from a record 4.43 billion francs in 1995, said there was a significant rebound in demand for stainless and flat carbon products in Europe.
It said Sollac and Ugine's order books, in particular, were full.
"The price charges are still low for the first quarter but some improvement can be seen, specifically in galvanized products, which should be confirmed in the spring," it said in a statement.

"Although annual contract negotiations reflected the adjustment in market conditions in 1996, the downward movement was limited in many cases," it said. Large customers WEre still anxious to maintain high technical product quality from their main suppliers.
